top_one.cause: In the masked round-robin winner branch, the one-hot grant uses masked_request_mask but the encoded grant uses the unmasked request_index. With all requests active, request_index stays 0 while masked winners rotate through ports 1, 2 and 3. The encoded output therefore disagrees with the correct one-hot grant.

evidence.observation: At 54 ns request=0xf, mask_reg=0xe, masked_request_valid=1, masked_request_index=1, request_index=0, but grant_encoded_next=0. At 56 ns the registered grant is 0x2 while grant_encoded=0; it must encode port 1.
At 46, 56, 66, 76 and 86 ns grant is respectively 0x1, 0x2, 0x4, 0x8, 0x1, while grant_encoded remains 0. This isolates encoded selection rather than round-robin one-hot scheduling.
Driver query identifies the output assignment at line 64, not the root cause. Source read shows masked winner branch at 116-124, faulty index selection at 119 and registration at 146.

Independent cyclic scan checks grant_encoded against chosen port. All seeds first fail encoded_grant at 56 ns while expected and actual one-hot grant both equal 0010; errors are 43, 42 and 42 for seeds 1, 7 and 42.

limitations: Waveform samples cover initial sustained contention in the live session. All three supplied failure logs were read; no new simulation or repaired RTL test was run. Other arbiter parameter combinations are not established by this evidence.

top_one.cause: The preload appends a constant 1 as the least significant shift-register bit. The right-shift transmitter consequently emits 1, then payload bits 0 through 6 in its eight data slots, losing bit 7. The constant belongs above the payload so that bit 0 is transmitted first.

evidence.observation: At 54 ns s_axis_tdata=0x35, tvalid=tready=1, bit_cnt=0. At 56 ns data_reg=0x06b, bit_cnt=9, prescale_reg=0xf, txd=0. This is exactly (0x35<<1)|1 loaded at the 55 ns edge.

At 214 ns data_reg=0x6b, prescale_reg=0, bit_cnt=9, txd=0. At 216 ns data_reg=0x35, prescale_reg=0xf, bit_cnt=8, txd=1. At 374 ns data_reg=0x35 and prescale_reg=0; at 376 ns data_reg=0x1a, bit_cnt=7, txd=1. The shift operation itself consistently emits the old low bit.

Data-slot center samples at 295,455,615,775,935,1095,1255,1415 ns give txd bits 1,1,0,1,0,1,1,0: byte 0x6b rather than input 0x35. At first error 455 ns bit 1 is 1 rather than 0. The spacing is the specified 160 ns per bit; txd is high at stop center 1575 ns.
trace_driver returns declaration line 69. Source inspection identifies preload at 97; line 105 shifts right into txd; counter allows eight such data shifts before explicit stop generation.
All seeds first fail serial_data_bit at 455 ns and complete 12 sent/received frames; errors are 38,45,51 for seeds 1,7,42.

limitations: Detailed waveform evidence is from the first frame of the live session. Repairs are proposed, not simulated; additional prescale values and DATA_WIDTH configurations were not tested. The fault statement is inferred from observed preload and shift behavior, not the driver declaration.

top_one.cause: The W-channel capture logic ignores incoming byte strobes and fills the stored strobe with ones. Partial writes therefore reach the register interface as full-width writes, even though captured address and data are correct.

evidence.observation: At 54 ns AWVALID=AWREADY=1 and AWADDR=0; at 56 ns AWREADY=0. At 74 ns WVALID=WREADY=1, WDATA=0xac000001, WSTRB=1, but s_axil_wstrb_next=0xf.

At 76 ns WREADY=0, reg_wr_en=1, reg_wr_addr=0, reg_wr_data=0xac000001 and reg_wr_strb=0xf. At 84 ns the same active register write retains strobe 0xf while the input strobe is 1. Address and data match the request; strobe alone differs.

Checker reports register_payload at 85 ns. It observes pre-NBA reg_wr_en=1 on the positive edge; settled waveform at 85 ns already shows reg_wr_en=0. The 84 ns sample establishes the payload seen by that checker without confusing pre-edge and post-edge values.

Driver query returns strobe register declaration at line 82. Source shows constant capture at 122, strobe registration at 139 and source assignment of reg_wr_strb to the stored strobe in the locally read RTL at 95.
All seeds report 12 payload errors with 12 sent and received. First errors occur at 85 ns for seed 1 and 95 ns for seeds 7 and 42.

limitations: Detailed waveform inspection covers the first write of the live session; supplied logs cover all seeds. No repaired simulation was performed. Wait/timeout behavior and arbitrary back-to-back traffic remain untested by this diagnosis.
